1520: They demanded our most important papers, skipped every queue, and were, I checked twice, on no list at all.
1521: They swept past every waiting official and asked for the VIP forms, though no one had heard of them.
1522: They acted more official than the officials. On no register anywhere, yet everyone stepped aside for them.
1523: They wanted the papers we reserve for heads of state and cut every line in the room to get them.
1524: Not on a single list. They insisted otherwise so grandly that half my colleagues began to believe it.
1525: They demanded stamps and seals for a person who, on all our paper, does not exist here at all.

1532: They asked for the paperwork we keep for royalty, produced no proof, and expected none to be needed.
1533: On no list, in no file — yet they signed my ledger as if they personally owned the whole building.

1536: They wanted every important form at once and treated the ordinary queue as a personal insult.

1542: They insisted on the grand welcome due a head of state, and that we all forget it ever happened.
1543: Full honors, the best suite, and please leave the guest book blank — all requested in one breath.
1544: They asked for every formality by name, then asked, sweetly, that the whole visit go unrecorded.

1554: They insisted every rule of welcome be followed, then asked me to leave their name out of all of it.
